newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia plans satellite city near Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia plans satellite city near Jakarta.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto on Wednesday approved plans to build a satellite city near the capital Jakarta that would be developed by his second son, Bambang Trihatmodjo.
"The president has approved the plan to establish a new city in Jonggol, West Java to anticipate future population growth," Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita told reporters.
The proposed city aims to spur regional economic growth and create employment opportunities that would help reduce the number of Indonesians in the outskirts working in Jakarta.
Jakarta, home to about 10 million people, has chronic traffic problems and is a haven for Indonesians, especially from rural areas, seeking a stable livelihood.
Ginanjar said the city will be located some 40 km (25 miles) south of Jakarta.
He said Jonggol city would be surrounded by houses, industrial estates, forests and plantations.
West Java Governor Nuriana told reporters after making a presentation to Suharto, that Bambang Trihatmodjo would develop the city.
Nuriana did not say when construction would start or how much the private project would cost.
